name: Kelvex TacSling Courier Bag MK-3
description:
Single-strap ballistic-nylon messenger bag in transit-authority grey with high-vis orange reflective piping along the flap seam. The body is reinforced at corners with vulcanized rubber bumpers. Interior is a dense foam-lined main compartment with a rigid document sleeve and a secondary mesh pocket sized for a compact medkit.

The shoulder strap is wide, padded, and routes over the chest with a magnetic sternum clip that releases under pressure — designed for quick dismount in crowded transit cars. Exterior has a waterproof map sleeve and two zippered side pockets.
functionality: Waterproof main compartment, rigid document sleeve rated for A3 flatfiles, chest-release strap for rapid dismount, exterior RFID-shielded pocket for transit passes and ID chips. Fits over chrome arm rigs without binding.
what_it_says: This person moves fast, carries what matters, and doesn't have time to look precious about it.
story_hooks: The MK-3 has a manufacturing defect in the RFID shielding — corporate knows, and chose not to issue a recall.
A courier's bag was found abandoned on a MagRail platform, interior pristine except for a handwritten list of names — all Tier 4 executives.
Street vendors near Circuit stations sell knockoff MK-3s with a hidden secondary compartment built into the foam lining.
related_entities: Ringo Heavy Transit MagRail Levitation Transport Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian single-strap messenger bag worn diagonally across the chest, presenting a compact but substantial silhouette. The transit-authority grey creates a deliberately inconspicuous urban aesthetic, while high-vis orange reflective piping traces the flap seam like circuit paths. Projects functionality and practical mobility.
physical_description.fit: Worn cross-body with the bag sitting at mid-torso. The wide, padded shoulder strap distributes weight evenly across one side. Designed for active transit use—fits close enough to prevent swing during movement but loose enough for quick access and emergency release.
physical_description.primary_material: Ballistic-grade nylon with vulcanized rubber corner reinforcements. Interior lined with dense foam padding.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, matte ballistic nylon exterior with a slight waxy finish for water resistance. Reflective piping has a subtle catch-light quality. Rubber bumpers are hard and slightly tacky. Padded shoulder strap is soft synthetic fleece against skin.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: transit-authority grey (neutral, corporate-utility tone). Accents: high-vis orange reflective piping along flap seam and edge-trim. Black zippers and hardware.
closures: Magnetic sternum clip on shoulder strap (quick-release design)
Main flap closure (likely hook-and-loop or magnetic)
distinctive_features: Vulcanized rubber bumpers at all four corners
Wide, padded shoulder strap with integrated magnetic sternum clip rated for pressure-release
Rigid foam-lined main compartment with structured document sleeve
Secondary mesh pocket sized for compact medkit
High-vis reflective piping for low-light visibility
Transit-authority grey colorway signals official utility
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional. A working-class courier or transit worker bag—quality construction without luxury branding. Accessible to gig workers, medical responders, and autonomous delivery operators.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals either courier/delivery work, transit authority employment, or street-level logistics. The quick-release sternum clip and medkit pocket suggest familiarity with high-traffic urban environments. Not quite military, but paramilitary-adjacent in design philosophy.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in with visible scuff marks on rubber bumpers. Reflective piping shows minor dulling from regular use. Interior foam retains impression patterns from frequent cargo. Strap padding is compressed but functional.
